entries.title: Confirm temporary build-artifact deletions
entries.description: Temporary build-artifact cleanup now follows each deletion with at most five read-only checks. Only HTTP 404 confirms absence; API errors and artifacts still visible at the limit remain failures with an artifact ID in the diagnostic.

entries.title: Reject outdated review-version checks
entries.description: Saved review-version lists now reject checks whose original window or project QA scope changed, whose dataset was replaced, or whose review was replaced or moved. Dataset and review refusals ask you to reload the list. Normal missing, changed and unreadable file results are preserved.

entries.title: List review attachment metadata within its project
entries.description: List the names, declared file types, sizes and SHA-256 digests of files attached directly to a review through local project queries. Comment-linked files, storage paths and file contents are excluded. Lists above the 1,000-file or 512 KiB JSON limit are rejected in full.

entries.title: Read user comments through local project queries
entries.description: Read a review's user comments through local queries confined to its project, preserving text and order. Prompts linked to agent runs, agent responses and structured evidence are excluded. Results above the comment or JSON size limit fail explicitly.

entries.title: Select all text before document-bound QA input on macOS
entries.description: Meta+A in the observed-document key tool now carries Chromium's Select All editing command on macOS. The matching key-up stays on the original surface, and a page can cancel the editing action. Text input still uses the actual focus and selection.

entries.title: Tie opt-in QA input to the observed web document
entries.description: The new optional QA document tool lets agents observe an in-app web view or owned popup and send input with its app-issued document ID. Navigation, renderer loss and target replacement invalidate old observations. Stale requests are rejected before input starts; later failure warns that input may have applied and must not be replayed. Paired releases stay on the original contents, and failed cleanup quarantines the window. The eleven legacy QA tools remain unchanged.

entries.title: Connect a fresh MCP process to a running app
entries.description: On macOS and Linux, a fresh MCP process can find one privately registered running app using a custom data folder when no explicit connection is selected and the default connection file is absent. The session stays tied to that app instance. Multiple or stale records require explicit selection. Windows automatic discovery is unsupported.
